questions.text:
A user starts browsing a webpage hosted at a remote server. The browser opens a single TCP connection to fetch the entire webpage from the server. The webpage consists of a top-level index page with multiple embedded image objects. Assume that all caches (e.g., DNS cache, browser cache) are all initially empty. The following packets leave the user's computer in some order.

(i) HTTP GET request for the index page
(ii) DNS request to resolve the web server's name to its IP address
(iii) HTTP GET request for an image object
(iv) TCP SYN to open a connection to the web server

Which one of the following is the CORRECT chronological order (earliest in time to latest) of the packets leaving the computer ?
questions.solution:
Order in which the packets leave the computer:
1. (ii) DNS request [latex]\text{---}[/latex] the IP address of the server is needed before anything else (caches are empty).
2. (iv) TCP SYN [latex]\text{---}[/latex] open the TCP connection with the server.
3. (i) GET index page [latex]\text{---}[/latex] first request on the connection.
4. (iii) GET image [latex]\text{---}[/latex] the browser knows about the image only after it receives and parses the index page.

Answer: (ii), (iv), (i), (iii)

questions.text:
Given an integer array of size [latex]N[/latex], we want to check if the array is sorted (in either
ascending or descending order). An algorithm solves this problem by making a
single pass through the array and comparing each element of the array only with its
adjacent elements. The worst-case time complexity of this algorithm is
questions.solution:
The algorithm compares each pair of adjacent elements once: [latex]N-1[/latex] comparisons in the worst case (when the array is actually sorted, it must check every pair before saying YES).

It cannot do less: any element not examined could break the order. So the worst case is [latex]\Theta(N)[/latex], i.e. both [latex]O(N)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(N)[/latex].

Answer: both [latex]O(N)[/latex] and [latex]\Omega(N)[/latex]

Each call of fX() reads one character and, if it is not newline, calls fX() again before printing. Each call has its own local [latex]a[/latex].

Calls read: '1' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '2' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '3' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '4' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '\n'. The last call reads newline, makes no further call and prints nothing.

While returning, the calls print their characters in reverse order: 4, 3, 2, 1. Then main returns normally.

Answer: The program will terminate with 4321 as output

questions.text: Let S be the specification: "Instructors teach courses. Students register for courses. Courses are allocated classrooms. Instructors guide students." Which one of the following ER diagrams CORRECTLY represents S?
questions.solution:
From the specification we need 4 entity sets [latex]\text{---}[/latex] Instructor, Course, Student, Classroom [latex]\text{---}[/latex] and 4 relationships:
Instructor-Teaches-Course, Student-Registers-Course, Course-Allocated-Classroom, Instructor-Guides-Student.

- (i): Registration is drawn as an entity and Student as a relationship [latex]\text{---}[/latex] wrong.
- (ii): no Student entity; an extra Projects entity is used [latex]\text{---}[/latex] wrong.
- (iii): Classroom is attached directly to Course and the Allocation relationship does not connect Classroom [latex]\text{---}[/latex] wrong.
- (iv): all four entities and all four relationships are connected correctly.

Answer: (iv)
